items.question_text: A lift motor transfers 36 000 J of energy to the lift in 2 minutes. What is the power of the motor?

feedback.a: This divides the time by the energy. Power is energy ÷ time: \(36\,000 \div 120 = 300\,\text{W}\).
feedback.c: This uses the time in minutes. Convert first: 2 minutes = 120 s, so \(36\,000 \div 120 = 300\,\text{W}\).
feedback.d: This multiplies energy by time. Power is the energy transferred each second: \(36\,000 \div 120 = 300\,\text{W}\).

items.explanation: Convert the time: 2 minutes = 120 s. Power = energy transferred ÷ time = \(36\,000 \div 120 = 300\,\text{W}\).

items.question_text: A conveyor belt motor has a useful power output of \(250\,\text{W}\). It runs for 90 s. Calculate the energy it transfers usefully in this time.

wrong.misconception: This divides the power by the time. Power = energy ÷ time, so energy = power × time: \(250 \times 90 = 22\,500\,\text{J}\).
This divides the time by the power. Rearranging P = E ÷ t gives E = P × t: \(250 \times 90 = 22\,500\,\text{J}\).

items.explanation: Power is energy transferred per second, so energy = power × time = \(250 \times 90 = 22\,500\,\text{J}\).

items.question_text: A student pulls a sledge 15 m across flat snow with a steady force of 120 N in the direction it moves. This takes 20 s. What is the student's power?

feedback.a: This multiplies the work done by the time. Power is work done ÷ time: \(1800 \div 20 = 90\,\text{W}\).
feedback.b: 1800 J is the work done (\(120 \times 15\)), not the power. Power is how fast the work is done: \(1800 \div 20 = 90\,\text{W}\).
feedback.d: This leaves out the distance. First find the work done, \(W = Fs = 120 \times 15 = 1800\,\text{J}\), then \(P = 1800 \div 20 = 90\,\text{W}\).

misconception_map.d: slip: divided the force by the time, leaving out the distance

items.explanation: Work done = force × distance = \(120 \times 15 = 1800\,\text{J}\). Power = work done ÷ time = \(1800 \div 20 = 90\,\text{W}\).

items.question_text: Why does the National Grid transmit electrical power at a very high potential difference?

options.a: It lowers the current, so less energy is dissipated in the cables
options.b: It raises the current, so the power reaches homes faster
options.c: A high potential difference makes the cables less likely to break
options.d: It increases the total energy the power stations produce

feedback.b: For the same power, a higher potential difference means a lower current, not a higher one.
feedback.c: The potential difference does not change the strength of the cables.
feedback.d: Power stations do not produce more energy because of the transmission voltage.

misconception_map.b: slip: thinks a higher voltage means a higher current for the same power
misconception_map.c: slip: confused electrical and mechanical properties of cables

items.explanation: P = VI: for the same power, a higher potential difference means a smaller current, and a smaller current dissipates less energy heating the cables.

items.stem: A [[machine]] transfers \([[E]]\,\text{J}\) of energy in \([[t]]\,\text{s}\). Calculate its power.

feedback.multiplied: This multiplies energy by time. Power is the energy transferred each second: \(P = \dfrac{E}{t} = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).
feedback.upside-down: This divides the time by the energy. Power = energy ÷ time: \(P = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).

items.question_text: A winch motor has a power of 500 W. What does this tell you?

options.a: It transfers 500 J of energy every second
options.b: It transfers 500 J of energy in total
options.c: It pulls with a force of 500 N
options.d: It transfers 500 J of energy every minute

feedback.a: Power is fixed for the motor, so the energy it transfers is fixed too: 500 J in total.
feedback.c: Power is measured in watts, not newtons; force is a different quantity.
feedback.d: The watt does not refer to minutes.

misconception_map.d: slip: wrong time unit for the watt

items.explanation: A power of 500 W means the motor transfers 500 J of energy.

items.question_text: Kofi and Ama have the same weight. They each run up the same flight of stairs. Kofi takes 5 seconds and Ama takes 8 seconds. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Their powers are equal, because each does the same amount of work
options.b: Kofi gains more energy, because he climbs the stairs faster
options.c: Ama has the greater power, because she works for longer
options.d: They gain the same energy, but Kofi has the greater power

feedback.a: They do the same work, but power is work done ÷ time. Kofi does it in less time, so his power is greater.
feedback.b: The same weight lifted the same height gains the same gravitational potential energy, however fast. Being faster means a greater power, not more energy.
feedback.c: Working for longer does not mean more power. Power is the rate of transfer: the same energy in less time is a greater power, so Kofi's is greater.

misconception_map.a: slip: ignored the time taken when comparing powers
misconception_map.c: slip: thinks a longer time means a greater power

items.explanation: Both lift the same weight through the same height, so both gain the same energy in their gravitational potential energy stores. Power = energy ÷ time: Kofi transfers that energy in 5 s, Ama in 8 s, so Kofi's power is greater.

items.question_text: Esi and Yaw weigh the same. Both climb the same staircase at school. Esi takes 6 seconds and Yaw takes 10 seconds. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Esi gains more energy, because she climbs the stairs faster
options.b: Yaw has the greater power, because he works for longer
options.c: They gain the same energy, but Esi has the greater power
options.d: Their powers are equal, because each does the same amount of work

feedback.a: The same weight lifted the same height gains the same energy, however fast. Being faster means a greater power.
feedback.b: Power is the rate of transfer. The same energy in less time is a greater power, so Esi's is greater.
feedback.d: They do the same work, but Esi does it in less time, so her power is greater.

misconception_map.b: slip: thinks a longer time means a greater power
misconception_map.d: slip: ignored the time taken when comparing powers

items.explanation: Both gain the same gravitational potential energy. Power = energy ÷ time, and Esi takes less time, so her power is greater.
